entries.title: Opening a shop of your own
q: how do i open a shop
how do i make a shop
can i have my own shop
how to set up a store
how do i sell things in my own shop
how to make a shop in the village
how do i run a shop
can i have more than one shop
entries.answer: A shop of your own is the easiest business: a room with a Shop Counter and stock in a chest, and folk come in to buy. Press U, then Open a shop.
more: You fill the shelves, folk come in and buy at the counter, the coin goes into its till.
No charter and no hands to pay; just a licence when you register.
steps: Press U → Open a shop: choose premises (a building of your own, have the town build it, or buy one for sale).
Building your own: any room with walls, a roof and a door onto a street or the square; set a Shop Counter in it (or hang a Shop Sign).
The shop's screen opens on Setup: name it, pick its kind and hours, and register (a licence of a week's rates, 3 coins at least).
Stock it: every chest, barrel, shelf and pot inside is stock. Set prices on Stock & prices.
Follow 'Getting started' on the Shop tab until the first sale.
controls: [Right-click] Shop Counter → Setup · Stock & prices · Books · Keeper
tips: Stock what folk here have a use for: the Stock tab says who would buy each ware and why.

Keep as many shops as you like, here and in other towns: each has its own room, counter, licence and keeper (you can't mind two counters at once), and the shop's screen has a button for each. A shop wants no standing, unlike a chartered business.
warn: Until the checklist is all ticks it stays shut: its sign says what it still needs.

entries.title: What a shop needs (the checklist)
q: no path from the door to a street
entries.answer: A shop stays shut until every line of its checklist is ticked. Open its screen from the counter: each cross says what's missing.
more: A shop opens only when everything is ticked: a counter, walls and a roof (the room is filled out from the counter, so a gap shows), a door, the door reached from a street or the square, a chest/barrel/shelf/pot of stock (not all back stock), ground a building may stand on (not a street or the mine), and its kind's kit (a bakery an oven, a butcher a smoker or oven, a tool shop an anvil or furnace, a clothier a loom, an apothecary a brewing stand, a tavern two seats).
steps: Open the shop's screen: each line is a tick or a cross with where to get it.
Fix the crosses; a line over the hotbar reminds you while you build nearby.
When it's complete you're told 'Your shop is ready to open!'
controls: [Right-click] Shop Counter → Shop tab → Getting started
tips: A door below the floor, or a blocked way out, fails 'reached from a street': the message names the door.

entries.title: Stocking a shop and setting prices
q: how do i set prices in my shop
how do i stock my shop
what should i sell in my shop
what do folk want to buy
entries.answer: Every chest, barrel, shelf and pot in the shop is stock. Set each ware's price on the shop screen's Stock & prices tab.
more: On Stock & prices, each ware has its price for a lot with − and + (Shift for ten), Going price and Keep back, how folk will take your price, and who would buy it and why.
Mark containers as back stock to hide them from customers (a keeper restocks from them).
steps: Put wares in the shop's chests.
Open Stock & prices and set each price (or press Going price).
Read the top line: how many wares have buyers in town, and what folk here want.
Restock what sells; drop what nobody has a use for.
tips: Folk buy only what they have a real use for now: their trade's tool, food for the household, a remedy, seed, a piece for the home.
Fair prices and full shelves raise the shop's name; dear prices and bare shelves lower it.

entries.title: Hiring a shopkeeper
q: can i hire someone to run my shop
how do i hire a keeper
who runs my shop when im away
entries.answer: A keeper serves at your counter in its hours and restocks the shelves, for a daily wage. Take one on from the shop screen's Keeper tab.
more: The Keeper tab lists folk who can be spared and their wage.
Taken on, a keeper stands behind your counter in its hours, greets customers and fills the shelves from the back stock.
It's paid its day's wage from the till each morning; the tab sets the wage against what the till takes a day.
warn: A keeper goes after two days' wages owed. Stock what sells first if the wage is more than the shop takes.

entries.title: Shop Sign
q: do i need a shop sign
entries.answer: A Shop Sign hung on a room's wall marks it as your shop and opens the shop's screen. Craft it from 2 planks and a sign.
more: A shop still needs a counter for customers to pay at.

entries.title: Starting a business (a charter)
q: how do i start a business
how do i make a business
how much does a business cost
entries.answer: A business is a firm of your own with its own hands. Press U, then Start a business: three steps (kind, premises, confirm) with the best already picked.
more: A kind (what the town is short of first, with the week's takings to expect).
Premises (your shop, a stall or a room the town lets, have the town build it, or buy a building).
Confirm: the charter fee (10 coins) and the building, with 'Borrow N and open it' if you're short.
steps: Press U → Start a business. On 'A kind', pick one (the first is 'A shop of your own, the easiest').
On 'Premises', choose where it works; for a new building, pick a drawing and a plot from the gallery.
On 'Confirm', check what's paid now and open it.
Then follow the welcome's next steps and run it from Your businesses.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Money → Start a business
tips: A chartered firm has hands of its own who make and sell its wares.
The town charters anybody it knows and has nothing against: a citizen, a friend, or a visitor who has said hello.
Start as many businesses as you like, of any kinds, in one town or several: each its own charter fee, premises and hands. Your businesses lists them all.
warn: A stranger nobody has spoken to is turned away: say hello to a few folk first (the step offers a button).

entries.title: Running your businesses
q: how do i run my business
how do i pay my workers
entries.answer: Your businesses page runs each firm: its hands, stock, prices and money. Press U, then Run it beside the firm.
more: Your businesses (U → Run it, or 'Show me my businesses') runs a firm by tabs: Summary, Hands (the best the town can spare, post an opening, take the best applicant), Stock (order its makings), Prices (its markup beside the going price), Money (invest, take drawings) and Shares & closing (the bourse, winding it up).
controls: Tabs: Summary · Hands · Stock · Prices · Money · Shares & closing
tips: Run several: Your businesses lists every firm you own with its till, this week's profit and its hands, a button to open each one's books, and Start another business.
A new player's firm has a week's grace; if it's in trouble you're told daily in chat what to do (coin in the till, stock, a hand).
With no business yet, the page explains the two kinds and has both ways in: Start a business and Open a shop.
warn: A firm owing more than it's worth, out of cash and credit, can be taken to court by its creditors after the grace.

entries.title: Every kind of business
q: what kinds of business are there
entries.answer: There are 18 kinds: makers, food and drink, and shops. Press U, then Start a business, to see the ones your town can have, best first.
more: Each wants a certain age and size of town, and a stall on the square or a room the town lets in its trade's building.
steps: U → Start a business: the kinds the town can have are listed, best for you first, with the reason and expected takings.
Pick one the town is short of (marked 'wanted').
tips: Wood Age kinds: toolsmith, carpenter, clothier, weaver, baker, fishmonger, greengrocer. Stone Age adds chandler, potter, glassworks, butcher, café, tavern, general store. Iron Age adds armourer, inn, apothecary, stationer.
The greengrocer and general store buy in at the market and sell on; the rest make what they sell.

entries.title: The makers: tools, armour, furniture, cloth, candles, pots, glass
entries.answer: The makers' businesses make what they sell: toolsmith, armourer, carpenter, clothier, weaver, chandler, potter and glassworks.
more: Toolsmith (stone and iron tools, shears, buckets; a stall; Wood Age, 10 folk).
Armourer (iron armour, shields, swords; a room; Iron Age, 18).
Carpenter (chests, barrels, beds, tables, frames, ladders; Wood, 10).
Clothier (leather clothes; Wood, 12).
Weaver (wool, rugs, banners; Wood, 12).
Chandler (candles, honey, comb; Stone, 12).
Potter (pots, bricks, terracotta; Stone, 12).
Glassworks (glass, panes, bottles; a room; Stone, 14).

entries.title: Food and drink: bakery, butcher, fish, café, tavern, inn, apothecary
entries.answer: The food and drink businesses: baker, butcher, fishmonger, café, tavern, inn and apothecary.
more: Baker (bread, cake, cookies, pies; Wood Age, 8 folk).
Butcher (cooked meats; Stone, 10).
Fishmonger (raw and cooked fish, its own catch; Wood, 8).
Café (stews, soups, baked potatoes; a room; Stone, 14).
Tavern (every café drink; a room; Stone, 14).
Inn (hearty meals; a room; Iron, 30).
Apothecary (potions, bottles, glistering melon; Iron, 20).
tips: A café, tavern and inn start with hands besides their founder.

entries.title: Shops: greengrocer, general store, stationer
q: what does a general store sell
entries.answer: The shops: the greengrocer and general store buy in at the market and sell on; the stationer makes its own paper, books and maps.
more: Greengrocer (carrots, potatoes, apples, beetroot, melon, berries; a stall; Wood Age, 12 folk) and General store (torches, lanterns, buckets, shears, flint and steel, rods; a room; Stone, 16) buy in at the market and sell on.

entries.title: Premises: a stall, a room, or a building
q: what premises does a business need
have the town build my shop
buy a building for my business
rent a room for my business
entries.answer: A business works from your own shop, a stall on the square, a room the town lets, or a building the town builds or sells you. You choose on Start a business's second step.
more: A business works from your own shop (checked against its kind), a stall on the square (its own once paid for), a room the town lets in its trade's building (a weekly rent), a building the town builds you (a gallery of drawings with quotes, times and a plot), or a building bought on the property market.
tips: A firm that does well takes larger premises.
A firm on your own shop pays the town no rent.

entries.title: Renting a market stall
q: how do i rent a stall
entries.answer: A stall is a booth on the square you rent by the week and fill with goods; folk buy from it. Ask any folk 'Rent a stall' (Trade, then Money).
more: A week's rent goes to the treasury (more in a bigger town; pay up to four weeks ahead).
Stock its barrel, set prices on its screen, and folk buy from it with their own coin into its till.
steps: Right-click its barrel and put in what you'd sell.
Crouch and right-click the barrel (or right-click its sign) for the stall screen: a price box per ware beside the going price, and how folk will take it.
Take the till on the screen whenever you like.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Money → Rent a stall
tips: Market day brings nearly everybody with coin to look.
Rent run out? It shuts; three days on it's given back, your goods and till kept for you. Nothing is ever lost.

entries.title: Service counters: buying at the shop, café, tavern, bank, smithy
q: how do i buy from the town shop
how do i buy food from the cafe
entries.answer: Shops, cafés, taverns, the bank and the smithy serve at a counter. Right-click it for its screen: prices, a basket and Buy.
more: Right-click a service point (the counter, or the keeper with coin in hand) for its screen: the keeper, hours, open or shut, your standing and coin.
At a shop: goods by kind with prices and why they move, Order what's not in, a basket with − and +, discounts, and Buy; Sell lists what the town buys from you.
steps: Find the counter: shop and store 7am-7pm, café 6:30am-8pm, tavern 4:30pm-1:30am, bank 7:30am-5:30pm, smithy and tailor 7am-6pm.
Or use Sell, Order, or the trade's own panel (mend, made to order, deposit...).
tips: Discounts: a friend, a citizen, a haggle or a medal; unwelcome players pay double.
The service counter block is three slabs over a barrel between two planks.

entries.title: A business's books
q: how do i see a business's profit
entries.answer: A business's books show its takings, costs, profit and what it sold. Open the town's books, then Economy, then Businesses, and click a row.
more: A business's books show its owner and hands and their pay; today, this week and all time (takings, costs, wages, rent, taxes, net profit, drawings); a fourteen-day chart; what it sold item by item and how each is made; its stock; what it bought; and why its prices moved.
The Businesses page lists every firm in town, a click to its books.
controls: [Right-click] an owner → Trade → Money → The books
tips: A business's books have Make an offer: name a price for the whole or a share; the coin waits in escrow till its owners answer.
Click any row of the Businesses page to open that business's books; Make an offer, Draw and Order work from there. Close (top right) or Esc leaves.

entries.title: Your business's data: sales, costs and charts
q: how do i see what my shop sold
how much profit am i making
how many did i sell per day
which of my businesses makes the most money
which of my businesses makes the most
how do i read my books
what does days of cover mean
entries.answer: Every business you own keeps its data: what it sold a day at a time, what that cost, its stock, its staff and its customers, in charts with a word of advice.
more: Overview: today, this week and all time: sales, costs, profit and margin, each with an arrow against last week; customers and sales a day; your best seller; your till; and a chart of takings a day with the profit line over it.

Sales: units and takings a day over 7, 28 or 56 days (the buttons at the top); hover a bar for that day's numbers. Under it every ware: how many a day, how many in all, the takings, the average price and its share. Click a column to sort by it.
Costs: each day's costs stacked: the stock you sold (what it cost you), wages, rent and tax, and the rest, with the day's profit as a line. Beside it, each as a part of your takings.
Stock: what is on your shelves, how many a day sell, the days of cover (how long the stock lasts at that rate: red under two), sales missed because a ware ran out, and how many to order for a week.
Staff: the hours it was open, the hours a keeper was behind the counter, each hand's days and wages, and your takings for each hour kept.
Customers: how many came, folk and players, how many came back, and the busiest hours of the day.
All businesses: with two or more, side by side: this week's takings, profit, margin, which way they are going and the till. Click one to open its data.
At the foot is advice from the numbers: a ware that keeps selling out, wages that eat the takings, stock that does not sell.
steps: Press U, then Your businesses.
Press Data beside a business (or beside your shop).
Pick a tab, or a range at the top: 7, 28 or 56 days.
Hover a bar or a row for its numbers; click a column to sort.
controls: A folk's profile → Business → Data › (a business you have a stake in)
tips: Margin is profit over takings. A margin under nought means the business lost money.
Days of cover tells you when to order: under two days is red.
The data is read off the same books the till is kept in, so its numbers and the till agree.
Others see only a business's week's takings and profit; the rest is the owner's.

entries.title: Folk's own businesses and competition
q: will folk compete with my shop
entries.answer: Folk open businesses of their own too, and compete with yours on price and name.
more: Folk open businesses of their own too, of the same kinds, when the town is short of something.
They compete on price and name: a folk buying its needs goes to whichever seller is the better buy (price, the walk, the shop's name), including your shop.

A folk whose business pays its way for weeks opens another: a branch of its trade or one beside it (the baker's café), up to four as its success carries it, never more than its fair share of the town's businesses. Each branch has a keeper of its own; a branch that loses money is shut. Its profile's Business tab lists every business it owns or works in, how each is doing, and what it means to open next.

entries.title: Opening Ribbon
q: how do i cut a ribbon
entries.answer: String an Opening Ribbon across a doorway and cut it with shears: the folk nearby cheer. Two string and a red dye make three.
more: A town's own ribbon across a great work is its leader's to cut at the opening.

entries.title: A farm of your own
q: orchard ranch woodlot fishery mine of my own
entries.answer: Hoe a field off the town's land, stand on it, and register it: U → Start a business → Register a farm. It becomes a business with books, land rates, tax on profit and outlets.
more: Sell through it at the price shown first: the town stores, a firm that sells it on, your own shop's stock, or a contract.
Only produce grown on its fields sells through it.
Hire folk hands (they pick salary or commission) or advertise for a player; a manager sells to the stores while you're away.
steps: Hoe and plant a field.
Stand on it: Register a farm (10c).
Harvest; then Sell: pick goods and an outlet, confirm the price.
Books: take your drawings.
controls: [U] → Start a business → Register a farm
tips: Its folk hands keep working while you're away; it idles only with no hands at all.

entries.title: Running your firm (hands, prices, selling)
entries.answer: Your businesses page: raise, cut or let go each hand (three days' severance), set a markup per ware, sell the whole firm, open a branch, and rescue it if its creditors take it to court.
more: The summary card shows this week's profit and loss against last week's.
Its folk staff keep it trading while you're away; a deputy manager also restocks and banks.
steps: U → Your businesses (or its Business Core) → Staff / Prices / Owners.
tips: Offers to buy it come to its Offers tab: accept, refuse or counter.

entries.title: Partners and contracts
entries.answer: Sell another player a share of your firm; profit splits by share and the majority decides. Contracts between players hold coin in escrow at the hall.
more: Post an advert for a player on the same jobs board, from your firm's or farm's Hands tab.
A disputed contract waits for the town's hearing.
steps: Your businesses → Owners → Offer the share.
U → Your businesses → Contracts with players → New contract.
tips: Miss a contract's day and the other side has its price back and your penalty.

entries.title: The Business Core
q: how do i see a shop's prices
entries.answer: Every business has a Business Core, a ledger desk at its premises. Right-click it: owners get the full hub, anyone else its public face (hours, wares, prices, staff).
more: Over it float its name, open or closed, and Deputy in charge when the deputy runs it.
Take yours up and set it elsewhere at the premises to move it; one to a building.
Breaking another's is a crime, and the business sets another next morning.
steps: Walk up to the desk with the little sign.
Right-click it.
Owners: follow the four-step tour the first time.
tips: Craft one from ink, a book, a sign, a chest and planks.

entries.title: A deputy manager
q: who runs my business when i log off
entries.answer: Folk staff keep your business open while you're away. A deputy manager also restocks, prices, banks and opens up, within your standing orders, as their character allows.
more: Choose what they may touch: a master switch, only while I'm away or always help, and a switch for each task.
They never override a price or target you set.
A report waits when you log back in; a dishonest one shows in the books.
steps: Staff tab: Set as deputy manager on a folk hand; pick a title and rise.
Deputy tab: flip the task switches; set the spending limit.
tips: Hardworking deputies open on time; easygoing ones don't.
warn: It shuts only if all its staff are players and none is online.

entries.title: Buying a business by offer
q: make an offer for a business
buy a share of a firm
entries.answer: Businesses are bought by offer, never one click: name a price for the whole or a share; the coin waits in escrow while its owners accept, refuse or counter.
more: The valuation guide shows book value, profit and goodwill; owners ask more than fair value.
Folk owners take half a day or more to answer, by their character; a lowball offends.
Refused, withdrawn or lapsed, your coin comes back.
steps: Its Business Core or its books: Make an offer.
Pick the share, price, terms and how long it stands.
Watch Offers you've made for a counter.
controls: Right-click its Business Core → Make an offer
tips: Some family firms aren't for sale at any price.

entries.title: Buying at a till (the checkout)
q: how do i buy from a shop
how do i buy more than one
how do i use the kiosk
how do i sell to a shop
entries.answer: Right-click a till (the brass register on a shop's counter), or the shopkeeper behind it. Press + and − for how many of each thing, check the total on the right, then Pay.
more: Every shop, café, bakery and player's shop has one. Shift-click + or − for ten at a time.
The basket on the right shows each line, any discount, the total, and the coin you carry (and what's in the bank here). If Pay is greyed it says why: short of coin, sold out, or nobody at the till.
With nobody behind the till it says when they're back, and offers self-service if the owner allows it. A Self-Service Kiosk always serves itself.
Over 50 coins it asks once more. What you buy goes in your pack, or at your feet if it's full.
If the business buys things, a second tab, Sell to them, works the same way: + and − on what you carry, at their price.
Folk shop at the same tills. The till's sign says who it's serving.
steps: Right-click the till (or the shopkeeper on duty).
Press + on what you want (shift: ten).
Check the total on the right.
Press Pay (Enter works too).
controls: [Right-click] Till or Self-Service Kiosk → the checkout
[Right-click] Shopkeeper at the till → the checkout
tips: Owners: set a till on your counter and a kiosk where you like. On your own till's screen you can switch self-service on or off; on a kiosk you tick which wares it sells.
An unwatched kiosk is trusting. Now and then a dishonest folk takes one more than it paid for, and the watch may catch it.
warn: You can't buy your own stock at your own till: take it off the shelf.

entries.title: Shop fittings: shelves, cases, crates and boards
q: how do i put things on a shelf
how do i get more customers
entries.answer: Shop fittings show your wares and bring more customers. Set them inside your shop or business, right-click to stock them, and customers click a ware on them to put it in their basket.
more: Display Shelf, Glass Display Case, Produce Crate, Larder and Clothes Rack each hold five lots, drawn on them, and count as the shop's stock.
The Price Board chalks up today's prices; the Basket Stand opens the checkout for anyone passing.
Your staff fill empty shelves from the stock chests, walking over to do it.
More fittings, kept full, mean more footfall: up to a third more customers. The Business Core shows it (Shop fit-out: 4 shelves, 1 case, price board: +12% footfall).
Folk-run businesses buy fittings for themselves when they have coin to spare.
steps: Craft a fitting (or buy one at a till, or order it at the town's shop).
Set it inside your shop or business premises.
Right-click it to stock it (sneak and right-click to see it as a customer).
controls: [Right-click] someone else's fitting → the checkout with that ware
[Sneak + right-click] your fitting → as a customer sees it
tips: Food keeps in a larder, clothes hang on a rack; a crate suits produce. Empty shelves count for less than none.
